bibl.title: Artificial Intelligence in Education: A Review

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: existence
span.quote: The study ascertained that AI has extensively been adopted and used in education, particularly by education institutions, in different forms.

span.label: artificial intelligence in education
span.quote: The purpose of this study was to assess the impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on education.

span.label: review
span.quote: A qualitative research approach, leveraging the use of literature review as a research design and approach was used and effectively facilitated the realization of the study purpose.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Machine learning infers each learner's capabilities and needs, which lets the system deliver personalised content, and that personalisation is what raises uptake and retention (i.e. improves learning).
span.quote: Students on the other hand, because AI uses machine learning as adduced from the different studies, are able to have a better and richer learning experience because AI uses machine learning to assess capabilities and needs, and subsequently, with the findings of such an analysis, develop and disseminate personalized or customized content, which ensures higher uptake and retention, thereby improving learning.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Automating administrative paperwork frees instructor time, which is then redirected to core instructional work, raising teaching quality.
span.quote: AI, has significantly reduced the paperwork and workload on instructors, particularly in the performance of various administrative functions, thereby enabling them to focus on their core mandate, instruction, dissemination of content and materials in line with the curriculum in place at the institution or nationally [11], [13].

span.label: The review's scope was deliberately restricted to three areas of education taken from a prior framework.
span.quote: Premised on a narrative and framework for assessing AI identified from a preliminary analysis, the scope of the study was limited to the application and effects of AI in administration, instruction, and learning.

span.label: One cited source is reported as defining the review's central term as two different kinds of thing.
span.quote: Embedded computers, sensors, and other emerging technologies have facilitated the transfer of artificial intelligence to machines and other items, such as buildings and robots [11]. Indeed, Chassignol et al. provides a two-faceted definition and description of AI. They define AI as a field and a theory. As a field of study, they define AI as a study area in computer science whose pursuits are aimed at solving different cognitive problems commonly associated with the human intelligence, such as learning, problem solving, and pattern recognition, and subsequently adapting [11]. As a theory, Chassignol et al. defined AI as a theoretical framework guiding the development and use of computer systems with the capabilities of human beings, more particularly, intelligence and the ability to perform tasks that require human intelligence

span.label: Differences between the collected definitions are described as near similar rather than reconciled.
span.quote: Other scholars and in other studies, the definition of AI provided brings to the fore near similar elements

span.label: The corpus is bounded by a journal bibliometric threshold.
span.quote: Initially, a total of 250 articles, published after 2009 were selected premised on the aforementioned criteria; matching the search key words and search strings and inclusion in a journal with an H-Index of 20 and above

span.label: AI - A FIELD AND A THEORY AT ONCE, ON ONE SOURCE'S ACCOUNT: reported as a study area in computer science aimed at solving cognitive problems, and also as a theoretical framework guiding the development and use of computer systems; a field of study and a theoretical framework are not the same kind of entity, and the review reports both without choosing
span.quote: Embedded computers, sensors, and other emerging technologies have facilitated the transfer of artificial intelligence to machines and other items, such as buildings and robots [11]. Indeed, Chassignol et al. provides a two-faceted definition and description of AI. They define AI as a field and a theory. As a field of study, they define AI as a study area in computer science whose pursuits are aimed at solving different cognitive problems commonly associated with the human intelligence, such as learning, problem solving, and pattern recognition, and subsequently adapting [11]. As a theory, Chassignol et al. defined AI as a theoretical framework guiding the development and use of computer systems with the capabilities of human beings, more particularly, intelligence and the ability to perform tasks that require human intelligence

span.label: the definitions of AI - CALLED NEAR SIMILAR: the review gathers characterisations from several authors and describes them as bringing to the fore near similar elements, which is a judgement that differences do not matter rather than a demonstration that there are none
span.quote: Other scholars and in other studies, the definition of AI provided brings to the fore near similar elements

span.label: the H-Index - A PROXY FOR REPUTABILITY, WITH THE INFERENCE WRITTEN DOWN: the review states that the higher the H-Index the more reputable the journal and its authors, and then uses a threshold of 20 as an inclusion rule, so the corpus is bounded by a bibliometric number standing in for quality
span.quote: and the higher the H-Index, the more reputable the journal and the authors published in the journal are

span.label: builds-on → Chassignol et al. (2018), 'Artificial intelligence trends in education: A narrative overview'
span.quote: These areas, which Chassignol et al. identify as the framework for analyzing and understanding artificial intelligence in education, will form the scope of this study.

span.label: artificial intelligence —is-a→ field of study
span.quote: Embedded computers, sensors, and other emerging technologies have facilitated the transfer of artificial intelligence to machines and other items, such as buildings and robots [11]. Indeed, Chassignol et al. provides a two-faceted definition and description of AI. They define AI as a field and a theory. As a field of study, they define AI as a study area in computer science whose pursuits are aimed at solving different cognitive problems commonly associated with the human intelligence, such as learning, problem solving, and pattern recognition, and subsequently adapting [11]. As a theory, Chassignol et al. defined AI as a theoretical framework guiding the development and use of computer systems with the capabilities of human beings, more particularly, intelligence and the ability to perform tasks that require human intelligence

span.label: artificial intelligence —is-a→ theoretical framework
span.quote: Embedded computers, sensors, and other emerging technologies have facilitated the transfer of artificial intelligence to machines and other items, such as buildings and robots [11]. Indeed, Chassignol et al. provides a two-faceted definition and description of AI. They define AI as a field and a theory. As a field of study, they define AI as a study area in computer science whose pursuits are aimed at solving different cognitive problems commonly associated with the human intelligence, such as learning, problem solving, and pattern recognition, and subsequently adapting [11]. As a theory, Chassignol et al. defined AI as a theoretical framework guiding the development and use of computer systems with the capabilities of human beings, more particularly, intelligence and the ability to perform tasks that require human intelligence

span.label: The review concludes that AI has been widely adopted across education institutions in several distinct technological forms.
span.quote: The study ascertained that AI has extensively been adopted and used in education, particularly by education institutions, in different forms.

span.label: Across the reviewed literature, AI raised the efficiency of instructors' administrative work such as grading, feedback and plagiarism checking.
span.quote: AI has improved efficiencies in the performance of different administrative tasks that instructors, would require a lot of time to perform in the absence of AI.

span.label: The main learning benefit identified was customisation and personalisation of curriculum and content to individual learners' needs and abilities.
span.quote: An important way in which AI has been applied in improving students’ learning is the customization and personalization of curriculum and content in line with the learners needs, abilities, and capabilities [15].

span.label: Only one reviewed study reported a negative effect of AI on education, namely erosion of academic integrity through paper-mill services.
span.quote: One study discussed or highlighted the adverse impact of AI, degradation of academic integrity and cheating using paper churning and paper mill services facilitated by AI.

span.label: artificial intelligence (Coppin's definition)
span.quote: Artificial intelligence, according to Coppin, is the ability of machines to adapt to new situations, deal with emerging situations, solve problems, answer questions, device plans, and perform various other functions that require some level of intelligence typically evident in human beings [4] (p.4).

span.label: H-Index
span.quote: An H-Index is an author level measure of scientific productivity in terms of publications and citations and by extension, contribution to science and scholarly pursuits; and the higher the H-Index, the more reputable the journal and the authors published in the journal are.

span.label: machine learning
span.quote: The core of machine learning is knowledge discovery, the process of parsing based on sampling data set known as ‘‘training data’’, generating meaningful patterns and a structured knowledge.

span.label: use of AI in education (in its different forms)
span.term: use of AI in education (in its different forms)
span.quote: This study seeks to assess how the use of AI, in its different forms, in education, has impacted or affected different aspects of education.

span.label: teaching, learning, and administration/management outcomes
span.quote: More particularly, the study will seek to assess how AI has affected teaching, learning, and administration and management areas of education.

span.label: 70% — share of the AI-and-education papers found in Web of Science and Google Scholar that were published in the 2015-2019 window
span.quote: Note that the papers published in 2015-2019 accounted for a large proportion, i.e., 70% of all the papers

span.label: 250 — number of articles initially retrieved that met the keyword and journal H-Index criteria
span.quote: Initially, a total of 250 articles, published after 2009 were selected premised on the aforementioned criteria; matching the search key words and search strings and inclusion in a journal with an H-Index of 20 and above.

span.label: thirty — final number of articles retained for analysis after the second screening round
span.quote: narrowing down the number of articles for analysis to thirty, a sample size that was considered sufficient to inform conclusions and inferences about the impact of AI on education

span.label: more than forty — number of documents (journal articles, professional publications, reports) selected after the eliminative process
span.quote: A total of more than forty articles, including journal articles, professional publications, and government and institutional reports were selected after the use of an eliminative process.

p.note: The full text of this article is not redistributable, so it is not included here. Every tag above carries the exact sentence it was made from, quoted under fair quotation. The article itself is at https://doi.org/10.1109/access.2020.2988510.
